title: Composite lifecycle commands: claim --start and finish --evidence --close
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: the common lifecycle takes several round-trips (claim, start, work, evidence add, finish, close); each gap between calls is an interleaving window where another agent can move state (the CONFLICT claim came from such a window), and each call costs an agent turn. Change: extend work claim with --start so claim+agent-start is one atomic runtime write returning the full handoff bundle, and extend agent finish so --evidence <ref-or-inline> plus --close performs evidence attach, finish, and close in one atomic operation with a single combined response (using the post-state embedding from the H1 mutation-response task). Note: work claim already reserves in one write and agent finish already supports some bundling — audit what exists first and close the remaining gaps rather than duplicating. Where: apps/cli/src/commands.ts, packages/engine/src/runtime.ts, command-registry.ts usage, docs/cli/COMMANDS.md, mirrored MCP tools. Constraint: composite failure must be atomic — a failed close must not leave a dangling finished-but-unclosed state without saying so explicitly in the response.
acceptanceCriteria: work claim --start returns the full handoff bundle from one atomic runtime write
agent finish --evidence --close attaches evidence, finishes, and closes in one call with one combined response
Partial failure of a composite is reported explicitly with the exact resulting state
